_readme: Capabilities Sealmetrics does NOT have, and which the docs must therefore never claim.
This is the third source of truth, alongside openapi-snapshot.json (does the endpoint
exist?) and ui-manifest.json (does the screen exist?). Those two validate references;
this one validates assertions. Every entry here was a real error found in published
content, so treat additions as cheap and removals as needing evidence.
Enforced by scripts/check-product-claims.mjs over docs/ and blog/.
id               stable slug, used in error messages and in allow[].
label            human name shown in the failure output.
why              the evidence that we don't have it. Cite the manifest or doc that proves it.
patterns         case-insensitive regexes that indicate the capability is being discussed.
allow            files where the term legitimately appears. Every entry needs a reason.
requiresSubject  only judge prose lines naming Sealmetrics explicitly. For capabilities
that come up constantly when describing the wider market.
The checker only fails on an AFFIRMATIVE claim. Mentioning a capability to deny it
('we do not track exit pages', 'Exit pages | ❌ No') is always fine, and in a
comparison table only the Sealmetrics column is read — competitors are free to have

unsupported.label: SSO / SAML sign-in
unsupported.why: Zero SAML or SSO paths in scripts/openapi-snapshot.json (261 paths). Confirmed by Rafa, Aug 2026.

allow.reason: Describes the CUSTOMER's identity provider as a referrer domain that breaks attribution. Not a claim about our auth.
Same: customer-side SSO domain as a passthrough referrer.
Same: customer-side SSO listed among passthrough referrer examples.
Describes Plausible's Enterprise SSO. Competitor capability.

unsupported.label: User journeys / navigation path analysis
unsupported.why: No path or journey endpoint in openapi-snapshot.json — /stats has pages, landing-pages and funnel only. No dashboard route either. Confirmed by Rafa, Aug 2026.

unsupported.label: Exit page tracking
unsupported.why: No exit-page endpoint in openapi-snapshot.json. Reconstructing exits needs per-visitor page sequencing, which the data model deliberately prevents.

allow.reason: Enumerates measurements the AEPD PERMITS, not what we implement.

unsupported.label: Session duration / time on page
unsupported.why: Absent from docs/reports/definitions.mdx and listed as not tracked in docs/faq/ga4-vs-sealmetrics.mdx. Requires following a visitor across page loads.

allow.reason: AEPD-permitted measurement list, not our feature set.

unsupported.label: Unique visitors
unsupported.why: docs/reports/definitions.mdx states plainly that Sealmetrics does not calculate unique visitors — any persistent per-user identifier would break the consentless basis.

allow.reason: AEPD-permitted measurement list.

unsupported.label: Shared / public dashboards as a product feature
unsupported.why: The API has five /shared-dashboards paths, but ui-manifest.json has NO matching dashboard route and nothing renders a shared dashboard. API-only building block; never present it as a shipped feature.

allow.reason: The API reference itself, which carries an explicit API-only caution.
Lists shared dashboards among v2 API additions. Endpoint-level statement, accurate.
Describes Plausible's shared and embedded dashboards, and our API-only status.

unsupported.label: IP-based geolocation
unsupported.why: Country comes from the browser timezone (docs/security-privacy/country-detection.mdx). The IP is never used for geo. This exact claim shipped wrong twice — via 'CloudFlare headers' in the GA post and in the pre-#63 privacy pages.

allow.reason: Describes the opt-in Agent Analytics GeoLite2 lookup used solely for bot detection, explicitly not attached to any hit.

unsupported.label: Session recording / heatmaps
unsupported.why: Never built, and structurally incompatible with consentless operation. Excluded by design, not by roadmap.

allow.reason: Plausible's self-hosting is a central point of the comparison.
Answers the self-hosting question and points to Matomo.
Describes the billing_enabled API field, whose false value covers self-hosted/grandfathered installs. Field semantics, not a product offer.
Lists 'Self-hosted Matomo, Sealmetrics' as alternatives; self-hosted qualifies Matomo.
Comparison page: self-hosting is Matomo's model, contrasted with Sealmetrics' managed cloud in the same sentence. Not a claim about us.
Comparison page: self-hosting is Matomo's model, contrasted with Sealmetrics' managed cloud in the same sentence. Not a claim about us.

unsupported.label: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 and other third-party security certifications
unsupported.why: Sealmetrics holds none. Removed from data-location.mdx and cnil-self-assessment.mdx in PR #58. Compliance rests on the architecture and the published self-assessments, which are our own assertions, not an auditor's.

allow.reason: States outright that we hold no such certifications. The disclaimer itself.
PCI DSS Level 1 refers to Stripe, our payment processor, not to Sealmetrics.

unsupported.label: Superseded data-loss / completeness figures (60-87%, 13-40%)
unsupported.why: Rafa's canonical figure is 15-60% of visitors lost by consent-based tools, depending on sector, brand and traffic mix (docs audit Aug 2026). The 60-87% and 13-40% numbers survived in scripts/llms-templates and contradicted the other 100+ mentions — the llms.txt header is the first thing an LLM reads about the domain.

unsupported.label: ISO 27001 / SOC 2 certification
unsupported.why: Sealmetrics holds no third-party security certification (CLAUDE.md). Denials are fine and expected; an affirmative line is a due-diligence lie.

unsupported.label: Analytics data hosted outside Dublin (Frankfurt / Germany)
unsupported.why: Customer analytics data lives in Dublin, Ireland only (CLAUDE.md). Seal AI Private prompts go to Scaleway in Paris — that is the single deliberate exception and is named Paris, never Frankfurt.

allow.reason: Names AWS Frankfurt as where *Claude* is served by a US-parent provider — a jurisdiction example about other vendors, not a claim about our hosting.

unsupported.label: gemma-4 / mistral-small described as the live Seal AI model
unsupported.why: Both were evaluated and replaced in July 2026; the live model is gpt-oss-120b on Scaleway (docs/lens/seal-ai/model-selection.mdx is the authority).

allow.reason: The authority page: explains why both were evaluated and replaced.
Benchmark results that compare the candidates, including the two that lost.

unsupported.label: Old metered LENS pricing (question quotas, €99 packs)
unsupported.why: LENS is free with BYOK; only Seal AI Private is paid (5M tokens/month, €358.80 per 5M-token pack). Per-plan question quotas and €99/500-question packs never existed (CLAUDE.md).

unsupported.label: Prompts sent to OpenAI / OpenAI as subprocessor
unsupported.why: Seal AI Private runs gpt-oss-120b (open weights, Apache-2.0) on Scaleway in Paris. OpenAI is not a subprocessor and prompts never reach it; "GPT" is the lineage, not the vendor (CLAUDE.md).
